transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-01-26
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood Eng), Leah (CTO, Sablebrook), Samir (SecOps), Marco (Infra), Aisha (Legal)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand Sablebrook's security gating for inference: SOC2/ISO expectations, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logs and retention, KMS/HSM usage, and whether Hosted/Dedicated/Private fits their procurement and compliance timelines.

Topics covered:
- High-level compliance posture (SOC 2, ISO 27001) and evidence required
- Identity and access: SSO (SAML), SCIM, RBAC needs
- Audit and telemetry: log retention, export, and who sees PII
- Encryption/KMS: bring-your-own-key (BYOK), HSM requirements, key rotation
- Deployment options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs
- Pilot/benchmark requests and procurement timeline (Q1 decision goal)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, uh thanks for carving time today, wanted to start with a quick round of intros because we got a couple people on from our side, priya's gonna be the se helping on architecture and ethan will chime on ops questions.
[00:12] Leah: hi, thanks. I'm Leah, CTO at Sablebrook. We're trying to evaluate inference vendors that can meet our retail PII controls and latency needs.
[00:20] Samir: Samir here, SecOps. Main things for us are SOC2 or ISO proof, SSO with SAML support and strong RBAC, and audit logs that we can ship to our SIEM. Also KMS integration is big, we need BYOK and HSM.
[00:34] Jordan: perfect, that aligns with a lot we see; just to level set, Redwood offers hosted API, reserved Dedicated capacity, and a Private deployment option with VPC and on-prem. On the compliance side we can provide SOC2 Type II report, ISO artifacts are available for some customers, and we support SSO/SAML with SCIM for user provisioning.
[01:05] Priya: yeah and from a control plane perspective, our RBAC is role-based with resource scoping by project and team, you can integrate it with your identity provider and map SAML groups to roles. There are a few edge notes e.g., on Dedicated you get more network isolation and can optionally terminate keys via your KMS.
[01:34] Marco: quick q on that - when you say terminate keys via our KMS, do you mean cloud KMS or an HSM-managed key? We need FIPS-backed HSM for certain payment flows.
[01:45] Ethan: short answer: we support AWS KMS BYOK flows today; for HSM-backed signing or external HSM we have partners and an HSM connector, but that is typically part of a Private deployment. There's some engineering work to wire up HSM signing endpoints.
[02:12] Samir: got it. Also auditing — how granular are your audit logs? we need to know per-token usage, which route/model was used, and operator/user who triggered calls. And retention — our policy is 7 years for some logs, but we might tier that.
[02:32] Priya: our Console exposes per-request metadata, and export hooks to forward logs to customer S3 or a SIEM; retention policies vary by deployment. On Hosted, we retain operational metrics for X days by default but can export raw audit logs on request; Dedicated and Private give you longer retention control. Note: raw transcript storage on Hosted is opt-in, can be turned off or redacted.
[03:03] Leah: when you say can be turned off, do you redact at rest or not store at all? We can't have customer PII stored externally for certain flows.
[03:12] Priya: correct — you can configure no persistence of prompt/response pairs on Hosted for a tenant, or route all logs to your S3 and then purge from Redwood side. That config is usually part of onboarding. There's a small tradeoff with analytics features.
[03:35] Marco: related to network — for Dedicated we assume we can do private peering into our VPC, do you support AWS VPC peering or PrivateLink?
[03:43] Jordan: yes both — Dedicated supports VPC peering and PrivateLink in our public regions; Private deployment gives you a private control plane and full air gap if needed. We'll need to look at egress patterns for software updates.
[03:58] Samir: procurement will ask whether you have SOC2 Type II and if the controls cover change management and incident response. Also ISO 27001 is a plus.
[04:10] Jordan: we have SOC2 Type II; I'll send the report. We also maintain an incident response playbook and can walk through it with your security team. For ISO artifacts I'll check which packages are available — some customers have ISO bundles via our enterprise agreement.
[04:29] Leah: awesome. A couple technical nitty gritty items - latency to our EU region matters for real-time checkout suggestions. What's the expected end-to-end p99 for small generative calls on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[04:42] Priya: p99s vary by model and seq length; typical p99 on Hosted for shorter generation is ~220ms in our EU region under normal load, Dedicated can get that down and give more consistent numbers under heavy throughput due to reserved GPU pools. We can run a short set of benchmarks using your prompts.
[05:03] Marco: please do. Also, do you support KV cache caching across pods? We have prompts with long context.
[05:11] Priya: yes, we support KV cache and prefix caching; sometimes the transcript reads 'KV cash' in logs but it's kv cache ;). There are config knobs for multi-tenant cache and you can pin sessions to a pool on Dedicated to ensure hot cache locality.
[05:30] Samir: going back to keys — rotation policy: if we push keys via BYOK to your platform, can we rotate without downtime?
[05:38] Ethan: we support key rotation with a grace window, typical pattern is dual-key validation for a short period to avoid downtime. For HSM-backed flows on Private we can do key rotation per your HSM vendor's best practice.
[05:53] Aisha: from legal — curious on data residency and contractual retention guarantees. You mentioned export hooks; is there a contractual way to require deletion and get cert?
[06:03] Jordan: yes we can add data deletion SLAs and provide attestations for deletions. For some enterprise customers we include a deletion confirmation artifact and audit trail. We'll need to capture the retention windows in contract appendix.
[06:20] Leah: excellent. Another question on SSO — does Redwood support multiple IdPs per org? we have different teams using different providers during a migration window.
[06:29] Priya: we do support multiple IdPs at the org level; mapping rules are flexible. Also SCIM support for provisioning and deprovisioning is available — but mappings need to be validated on onboarding.
[06:45] Samir: If we map groups to RBAC roles, can we limit who can deploy models or change rollout policies? we want separation of duties.
[06:53] Priya: yes, roles are fairly granular: admin, ops, developer, read-only. Model rollout and canary controls are restricted to admin/ops roles by default and you can create custom roles.
[07:08] Marco: one more infra question — how do you handle secrets for models (e.g., external connectors)? are those encrypted with customer keys or Redwood-managed KMS?
[07:17] Ethan: secrets in the platform are always encrypted at rest; on Dedicated we can enable customer-managed KMS to wrap those secrets. For Hosted default is Redwood KMS unless BYOK is enabled.
[07:34] Leah: okay. timeline: procurement wants a vendor that can meet our compliance gating by end of Q1. We're trying to decide between a Hosted pilot and going straight to Dedicated. Any recommendations?
[07:47] Jordan: many customers start with Hosted to accelerate proof-of-value and then move to Dedicated once they need predictable SLOs and stronger isolation. Given your BYOK and HSM constraints, we might pilot on Hosted with no-persistence and exported logs to your S3, then evaluate Dedicated within the 60-day pilot. If HSM is mandatory for production, Private/Dedicated will be the expected path.
[08:12] Samir: for pilot scoping, we'll need a config doc listing what data is stored where, exact retention windows, and a list of requested logs.
[08:20] Priya: we'll produce a pilot spec and config options — includes batching, quantization recommendations to control cost, and model variants. We'll also include a quickstep for running a latency/cost matrix.
[08:35] Aisha: we will need to review any subprocessing/subprocessor lists and a standard DPA. Can you share your standard DPA and list of subprocessors?
[08:43] Jordan: yes I'll include our DPA and a high-level subprocessors list. We can mark which ones are optional for Dedicated.
[09:00] (background cough)
[09:05] Leah: anything else?
[09:07] Marco: curious if you provide tamper-evident audit logs or append-only storage? Our compliance folks favor append-only for some trails.
[09:15] Priya: we have append-only audit streams and you can get a signed export for retention. For higher assurance, we recommend Private with your own storage endpoints.
[09:28] Samir: last thing: incident response — how are incidents triaged and how fast is the SLA for incident notification?
[09:35] Jordan: we have a 24x7 oncall for P1s, we notify customers per contract timelines (usually within 1 hour for P1) and provide post-incident reports. We'll share the IR playbook.
[09:50] Leah: ok good.
[10:00] Jordan: wrapping up — action items we'll send SOC2 and DPA, priya will scope the pilot and bench, marcos will share infra details, legal will list retention needs. Any blockers to scheduling the tech deep dive next week?
[10:18] Marco: available 2027-02-04 afternoon UTC.
[10:22] Priya: noted, I'll propose times.
[10:25] Aisha: legal will review docs as soon as they are up.
[10:30] Jordan: great thanks everyone. We'll follow up with a one-pager and the SOC2 link.

(Transcript notes: occasional mis-attribution to "Speaker 3" in auto-transcript, and some words mis-captured — e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache; "H S M" split into letters in some lines.)

End of meeting.
